origin.note: Centre of the sarsen circle. Method: circle fitted to 15 OpenStreetMap-mapped sarsen upright positions (radius 15.6 m, scatter 0.54 m) gives 51.178859, -1.826208; independently, NGR SU 12244219 (English Heritage 2010 survey report header, 10 m resolution; +5 m/+5 m cell centre converted OSGB36->WGS84 by a 7-parameter Helmert, ~3-5 m) gives 51.17886, -1.82621; Gazetteer of Great Britain lists SU 1224 4219 = 51.178887, -1.8262196; Wikipedia 51.17889, -1.82611. Heel Stone check: OSM centroid 78.8 m from this origin at azimuth 51.0 (Wikipedia: 77.4 m). Uncertainty: about +/-2 m relative to the mapped stones, +/-5-10 m absolute (OSM/Bing imagery registration, Helmert, 10 m NGR resolution). The brief's provisional 51.17888, -1.82619 is 3 m away: consistent.

datum.note: Local height = metres above Ordnance Datum minus 60. EU-DEM 25 m gives 101.4 m OD at the centre (EH survey control points around the monument read 99.8-104.8 m OD), so the ground at the stones is ~41.4 m local (fit: 41.6). The lowest DEM ground (the Avon, ~62 m OD) is ~2 m local, right at the engine's MIN_LAND clamp of 2 m: if river banks flatten, use offsetOD 55 (stones ~46.5).

boundsNote: Recommend x -2700..3700, z -2800..2200 (6.4 x 5.0 km): the extra 200 m east keeps the Avon's eastern meander (x to 3620, z -500..0) and Durrington village (x 3591, z -2284) in the scene; with the brief's xMax 3500 the Avon valley is cut by the edge there and the fit is ~12 m off. Outside even the recommended bounds: Robin Hood's Ball (x -2004, z -3766, ~1 km beyond the north edge), the long barrow at x 543, z -3143 (OSM node, far north), most of the Wilsford barrow group (z > 2200), Bulford (x ~4750), the summit of the Larkhill rise (z ~ -2950). Inside: Lesser Cursus, Winterbourne Stoke crossroads group (x -1900..-2280), Lake barrows (z to 2125), Woodhenge, Durrington Walls, Vespasian's Camp, Amesbury, Bluestonehenge, Coneybury, Cuckoo Stone, Cursus, King Barrow Ridge, Normanton Down.

sarsen-circle-centre.note: origin; centre of circle fitted to 15 OSM-mapped sarsen uprights (radius 15.6 m, scatter 0.5 m); agrees with NGR SU 12244219 (EH 2010)

heel-stone.note: OSM stone way centroid (ref 96); Wikipedia 51.179305,-1.825302 and 77.4 m from centre

avenue.note: centre line of the ditch-bounded Avenue polygons mapped in OSM (stones to the elbow near x 455 z -390, then east over King Barrow Ridge to x 1650 z -60) joined to the OSM footway "The Avenue" SE to the Avon; last leg (to Bluestonehenge) is a straight extrapolation of ~190 m. Ditches ~20 m apart (EH 2010 survey).

avenue-elbow.note: where the NE-trending straight stretch ends and the Avenue turns east (EH 2010: ditches turn sharply east after >550 m, in Stonehenge Bottom)

cursus-greater.note: outline from OSM (NPE-traced earthwork); Wikipedia: ~2.76 km long, ~100 m wide, up to ~150 m at the west end. Width here = distance between mapped long sides.

cursus-lesser.note: OSM outline (Bing); Wikipedia: ~400 m x 60 m, WSW-ENE; cropmark only

durrington-walls.note: centre from SU 1500 4376 (Gazetteer of Great Britain: 51.192885,-1.786628), Wikipedia 51.1925,-1.7875; OSM node is ~190 m off. Ring = ellipse 466 m E-W x 490 m N-S (Gazetteer: 510 x 535 yd) drawn as 16 points: APPROXIMATE, not a survey outline; centre uncertainty +/-60 m, outline +/-40 m.

durrington-southern-circle.note: position estimated (south-east part of the enclosure, near the SE entrance); +/-60 m. Wikipedia text says the circle is 70 m north of Woodhenge, which does not fit the enclosure ellipse above; unresolved. Do not rely on better than ~100 m.

woodhenge.note: OSM polygon (54 m wide) marks the post-ring area; Wikipedia: whole monument 110 m across incl. ditch (up to 12 m wide) and outer bank; six oval post rings; entrance NE; Wikipedia 51.1894,-1.78576

coneybury-henge.note: OSM outline; Neolithic henge excavated 1980s; (Coneybury Anomaly pit site is nearby, not mapped)

bluestonehenge.note: West Amesbury henge on the Avon bank; OSM marks it "approximate location from photos"; Wikipedia 51.1714,-1.7980; ditch ~25 m wide, stone circle ~10 m across (possibly 27 stones)

robin-hoods-ball.note: about 4 km NNW of the stones; Wikipedia 51.2128,-1.8550

vespasians-camp.note: OSM outline (rampart line, 14 vertices) re-sampled to 24 points at equal arc length (corners slightly rounded). Wikipedia: 14 ha, 730 m N-S, 374 m wide at the south, 100 m at the north; bank up to 40 m wide, ditch up to 10 m, counterscarp 18 m; Avon runs along the south side (sic: OSM puts the loop west and south)

amesbury-church.note: St Mary and St Melor (building polygon centroid); Grade I; may be the surviving priory church (Wikipedia Amesbury Abbey)

amesbury-abbey-house.note: OSM building "Amesbury Abbey": the 19th-century country house (Wikipedia: priory was destroyed at the Dissolution); not the medieval priory church

amesbury-abbey-precinct.note: NO source gives the precinct boundary. 220 x 130 m rectangle centred ~45 m west of the church (Fontevraud priory lay by the church). Placeholder only: lead should label as conjectural.

stonehenge-bottom-label.note: OSM place=locality node "Stonehenge Bottom" (label position only; the valley is fitted from the DEM)

stonehenge-bottom-axis.note: axis of the fitted Stonehenge Bottom valley (hand-drawn from the DEM minima, N-S at x ~ 430-750 m, deepening south); the Avenue crosses it near x 500-600, z -390; valley floor ~86-90 m OD there vs 108-111 m OD on King Barrow Ridge

terrain.note: Least-squares fit (Levenberg-Marquardt, numpy) of the terrain.ts formula (base + slope + sum of gaussian hills - sum of gaussian valleys by distance to a polyline; the engine adds +/-0.6 m micro-relief and clamps at 2 m) to 1,302 EU-DEM 25 m samples: a 200 m grid over x -2800..3600, z -2900..2300 plus a 50 m grid over x,z -500..500. Local datum = metres above OD minus 60 (OD = Ordnance Datum Newlyn). Valley polylines were set by hand from the DEM (dry valleys) and the OSM River Avon centreline (simplified to 60 m); hill positions were left free but boxed around the named feature. The ground within 60 m of the stones was constrained (extra weighted pseudo-samples at 41.3) so the megalith ground varies by <1 m over 50 m radius; without it the DEM itself varies ~2 m there. Fit is a schematic reconstruction: RMS 4.5 m over the bounds (43 of 1,186 samples are >10 m off, mostly at the margins and along the steep Avon scarps at Vespasian's Camp), RMS 3.1 m (max 6.9) within 500 m of the stones. The DEM is a modern surface model (includes woods, roads, the A303 and A344 cuttings, buildings); prehistoric relief was essentially the same at this scale. Slope is negligible (0.002); relief comes from the hills/valleys.

fit.crossCheck: EU-DEM vs Open-Meteo (Copernicus 90 m) differ by RMS 2.6 m (max 16.9) over the 1,302 points, mean +1.0 m; the fitted model vs Open-Meteo has RMS 5.3 m in bounds, so the fit error is of the same order as the disagreement between the two DEMs plus smoothing.
